tool_args.rationale: Across eight rows, y/u_now is consistently about 2.1 despite wide variation in x_now and mem_conv, supporting uncoupled Kelvin–Voigt creep. Fit its two positive parameters numerically to all observations. The previous submission failed only because predict referenced an undefined training-row global; this implementation stores fitted parameters in fit before fresh predictions.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; eight rows show the same response across differing x_now and mem_conv, so another batch is not needed to identify this uncoupled law.
Its predicted output changes with x_now, whereas the observations track u_now with nearly constant y/u_now despite large x_now variation.
A present-snapshot nonlinear function of u_now alone does not explain the systematic proportional scaling across the observed u_now range as simply as the supplied Kelvin–Voigt law.
Irrelevant to the observed response and explicitly not useful for resolving this model choice.
